children: plunged 15.2% in Wednesday's trading as UBS downgraded the Brazilian petrochemical company to Sell from Neutral with a $1.50 ADR price target, slashed from $4, citing persistent headwinds from spreads and restructuring.

UBS is late on the downgrade, analyst Tasso Vasconcellos acknowledged, but he still sees "no easy way out as spreads have broadly returned to the pre-conflict outlook," with material capacity additions in China outpacing demand growth in 2027-28, likely keeping spreads at low-cycle levels until later in the decade, with limited upside risk.

indebtedness and restructuring needs, with potential solutions carrying material dilution risk for shareholders; the company carries $13.2B in total debt, representing 95% of its total capital, while burning through cash with negative free cash flow of $1.7B over the last 12 months.
The analyst said he expects pressured EBITDA and higher free cash flow to equity consumption in the coming years, which could potentially require a more significant capital structure solution.

title: Braskem sinks as UBS cuts to Sell as Chinese capacity additions keep spreads under pressure
